description: The provided pie chart visually categorizes character types into two primary groups: “Virtual Characters” and “Real Characters,” with an additional distinct segment for “Custom Characters.” The “Virtual Characters” category, represented by a large light blue segment, dominates the chart and is further subdivided into five subcategories — Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, Game Characters, and an unlabeled segment at the top — all rendered in varying shades of light blue. The “Real Characters” category, shown in green, is composed of six subcategories: Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, and Influencers, each labeled and displayed in different shades of green. The “Custom Characters” segment, colored pink, stands alone as a distinct category between the virtual and real character groups. The chart uses color-coding and spatial separation to distinguish between these major categories and their subcomponents, though no numerical percentages are displayed, making the proportions qualitative rather than quantitative. The overall structure suggests a hierarchical classification system for character types, likely intended to support the paper’s focus on act-adaptive reward modeling for role-playing language agents by providing a taxonomy of character sources.
